description: Make same-work-item Workflow cleanup turns wait for terminal runtime facts to finish outbox delivery before admission, without weakening cross-attempt or server-side fail-closed validation.

tasks.title: Add an event-driven Workflow session delivery wait
tasks.description: Extend the runtime-event outbox port and implementation with a bounded, cancellable wait keyed by the cleanup attempt's immediate predecessor: the original Workflow scheduling identity for attempt 1, or the prior deterministic cleanup operation id for attempt 2+. Resolve waiters from durable record-removal settlements across workflow-session, workflow-cleanup, and Session-scoped session-followup records without polling or mutating delivery state, and expose a typed timeout carrying predecessor evidence and the exhausted budget.
acceptanceCriteria: The outbox exposes awaitCleanupPredecessorDelivery for projectId, workflowRunId, sessionName, cleanupAttempt, and precedingCleanupOperationId plus budgetMs and AbortSignal; attempt 1 selects retained workflow-session records for the Workflow scheduling identity, while attempt 2+ selects the prior workflow-cleanup boundary and every Session-scoped session-followup record carrying its deterministic cleanup operation id.

A wait completes immediately when no predecessor record is retained; attempt 1 covers every retained workflow-session record for the scheduling identity, and attempt 2+ remains pending for correlated session-followup runtime input and terminal activity even after the Workflow-keyed cleanup boundary has settled.

Pending waiters resolve only after the applicable removal snapshot has committed for acknowledgement settlement or deterministic binding-refusal settlement, or after recovered-state loading establishes that no predecessor record remains; a failed persistence attempt does not report delivery completion, and retention-cap drops are not described as acknowledgements.
Registering a pending waiter may kick the existing delivery path once, but no timer polls or re-evaluates retained state and no server session-status or delivery-status request is introduced.

Budget expiry rejects with a typed error containing projectId, workflowRunId, sessionName, cleanupAttempt, preceding cleanup operation id when present, and budgetMs, while caller abortion rejects promptly and cleans up the waiter and timer.
Waiting does not remove, reorder, rewrite, or otherwise mutate retained records and does not change acknowledgement policies, batching, ordering, retry, snapshot, or retention behavior.

Runner fake-timer tests cover immediate completion, original-turn acknowledgement-driven completion, attempt-2+ waiting on a prior cleanup boundary plus correlated session-followup runtime input and terminal activity, unrelated cleanup records not blocking, timeout evidence, cancellation, settlement persistence failure, and the absence of polling; the focused outbox tests pass.
tasks.output: Updated runtime-event outbox ports, scheduling-identity support, implementation, typed timeout, and fake-timer regression tests in packages/runner.
tasks.notes: Keep the port method optional for existing test doubles, but implement it in the production outbox. Derive the prior operation with workflowCleanupOperationId(workflowRunId, taskRunId, workId, cleanupAttempt - 1); do not change the Session-scoped ownership or delivery key of session-followup records. Use the injected RuntimeEventOutboxTimer only for timeout failure, not periodic state checks, and preserve snapshot version and delivery semantics.

tasks.title: Admit cleanup turns after terminal-fact delivery
tasks.description: Wire the outbox predecessor-delivery wait into the OpenCode and Pi admission paths for positive same-work-item cleanup attempts before opening the Workflow AgentSession. Attempt 1 waits for the original Workflow turn; attempt 2+ waits for the immediately preceding cleanup boundary and its Session-scoped terminal facts. Skip the runner-side unsettled projection guard only for those cleanup turns, preserve the authoritative server validation, and surface exhausted waits through a declared structured cleanup failure instead of a generic worktree or unsettled-session error.
acceptanceCriteria: For a positive OpenCode cleanupAttempt with a bindable Workflow identity, the Runner waits on projectId, workflowRunId, the exact session name used by openWorkflowAgentSession, cleanupAttempt, and the deterministic prior cleanup operation when cleanupAttempt > 1 before opening the session; once delivery settles, it submits the existing cleanup prompt to the same runtime session even if the pre-wait projection was active or unknown.

For a positive Pi cleanupAttempt with a bindable Workflow identity, the Runner derives the same predecessor after resolving the context session name and waits before opening the session or enqueueing session.cleanup, so frozen-binding admission occurs only after the original turn or immediately preceding cleanup turn is terminal server-side.

The OpenCode unsettled-session projection guard is bypassed only for a positive same-work-item cleanup attempt; every non-cleanup or cross-attempt turn retains the existing session-binding-failed behavior and fail-closed message for active or unknown prior sessions.

When no record is retained for the selected predecessor, both runtime paths proceed without added delay or a new server status round-trip, and cleanup admission does not re-consult the session-activity projection as a gate.

A delivery-wait timeout becomes session-delivery-wait-timeout with evidence naming the awaited project/workflow/session identity, the work item, and the exhausted budget; mohist/opencode and mohist/pi declare the code, and worktree enforcement preserves that code, message, and cleanupAttempts instead of collapsing it to worktree-dirty.
The default delivery budget is the bounded 60000 ms code constant and is injectable through the existing capability/action dependency plumbing for tests without adding runner configuration.

Cleanup prompt text, maximum cleanup-attempt accounting, clean-worktree completion requirements, and the server cleanup route and frozen-binding validation remain unchanged; every allowed attempt remains usable under predecessor delivery lag, and task success or failure continues to follow the actual cleanup result.

Runner fake-timer and admission tests cover OpenCode and Pi delivery lag for attempt 1 and attempt 2+, including a retained prior-cleanup session-followup terminal fact after the Workflow-keyed boundary settled; already-delivered facts; ordering of wait before open and cleanup submission; timeout evidence and manifest validation; maximum-attempt accounting; actual cleanup success/failure; and preserved cross-attempt fail-closed behavior. The focused Runner suites pass.
tasks.output: OpenCode and Pi cleanup admission integrated with the outbox wait, declared timeout failures, worktree-result preservation, and end-to-end Runner regression tests.
tasks.notes: Use request.session ?? work.workId for OpenCode and sessionNameFromContext for Pi. For cleanupAttempt > 1, derive the immediately preceding operation from workflowRunId, non-empty taskRunId, workId, and cleanupAttempt - 1; the existing cleanup reporter prerequisites make that identity available. A missing optional wait method retains current behavior for lightweight test doubles. Do not modify Server code or weaken cleanup frozen-binding validation.
